§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. Every open document costs an instance threads and memory
(`tools/proof/README.md`, "Relaunch the instance between proof sessions", has
the measured cost and what closing one gives back): a proof that closes what
it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and one that does not
relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument. A mutant's anchor is counted by `tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py` in
  `make test`: a proof taking `--mutant` holds its mutants in a top-level
  table (tree text as file, anchor, replacement; switches as names), and a new
  table shape or a mutant with no tree text gets its row there in the same
  change, and a table's expression stays pure, because the check evaluates it.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. Its scale is
`-RCDevCaptureScale 1|2|3` (spec §11 #539), which `screens.py` pins to 2, so a
capture is 2× on a 1× display without moving a window. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A proof that
compares with the base's built APP (`co2a_proof.py` D15, `ramp_proof.py` U1)
finds its base with `tree_copy.default_base()` and builds it whole with
`tree_copy.make_base_copy`; it never pins a commit's `app/` against the
tree's core. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

GitHub Issues on `kpgalligan/framejob`, through the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.
**Every issue an agent creates carries the `ai-drafted` label**, beside any
triage label: `gh issue create --label ai-drafted …`. **It also carries
`low-priority` unless it is urgent** — data loss or a corrupt project reachable
in ordinary use, a crash or hang reachable in ordinary use, a secret leak, or

# Plan: Tips (dialog, toolbar button, automatic ask, Settings section)

Tree: `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-tips` (branch `tips`, 34c7fea2, clean). Every path
below is relative to it. No STOP: the choices only the owner can make are under "Owner choices",
each with the recommendation this plan builds on.

## Goal

1. **Dialog.** One small dialog that says plainly who a tip funds (one developer, an open-source
   app), with "Leave a Tip" opening `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` (one constant) and
   "Not Now".
2. **Toolbar button.** A green "Tips" button right of Export… in the editor toolbar that shows
   the dialog, removable by deleting one file and one line.
3. **Automatic ask.** The dialog shown by itself, once per due moment: first after 30 days and 5
   exports a person made, then once a year in December, skipping a December that starts less
   than six months after the last ask. Never in an agent- or proof-driven instance.
4. **Settings.** A Tips section whose toggle turns off the automatic ask and removes the toolbar
   button, and whose own Tips button always shows the dialog.

## Owner choices (planned on the recommendation)

| # | Choice | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Exports before the first ask | **5** |
| O2 | What "30 days of use" counts from | **The first export a person completed from the export card**, 30 × 24 h elapsed. Not first launch: a launch is also what `framejob-mcp` and every proof do, so a key stamped at launch would count agent-only use and trip `DEFAULTS MOVED` on a fresh domain. Not "30 distinct days used": a casual user would wait a year. |
| O3 | "December" and "six months" | Any moment whose month is December in the **Gregorian calendar in the Mac's current time zone**. A December is skipped **whole** when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask (so: last ask after 1 June 00:00 of that year skips it). Judged whole so the ask cannot appear on, say, 30 December because the last one was on 30 June. |
| O4 | Dialog form | **Its own small window** titled "Tips" (the Settings window's mould), not a sheet and not an app-modal alert. It needs no host window (Settings and the Welcome state have no document), it cannot block a window or a tool call, and it adds no sheet site to the menu inventory. |
| O5 | When the automatic ask appears | Only when an export a person confirmed in the export card completes: for Export…, when its result sheet is closed (Close or Show in Finder); for Add to Queue, when the job completes. It is ordered front **without taking key**, so Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip". |
| O6 | What counts as "asked" | The automatic ask being shown, and a press of "Leave a Tip" from any door (someone who just visited the page is not asked again that December). Opening the dialog by hand and choosing Not Now records nothing. |
| O7 | The green | `DS.forest` (#1F8564, the brand mark's green, `Theme.swift:40`) with the white `DS.onAccent` label: 4.57:1, the same in light and dark, as the recorder's coral Record button is. `DS.action` is reserved to the action lane (CI-4). |
| O8 | Wording (drafts, American spelling, held by `ai_docs_r2c_proof.py` T1) | Window title "Tips". Heading: "Frame Job is free and open source". Body: "Frame Job is made by one developer. It is free to use and its source is open. If it is useful to you, a tip helps pay for the time to keep working on it. Tips are voluntary, and nothing in Frame Job is locked without one." Hint: "You can turn this reminder off in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Tips." Buttons: "Not Now", "Leave a Tip". Settings blurb: "Frame Job is free and open source, made by one developer. Tips are voluntary." Checkbox: "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder". Toolbar tooltip: "Support Frame Job". |

Counting continues while the toggle is off (two local numbers; turning it back on then behaves
sensibly). The in-app Assistant's `export` is the agent's door and does not count.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

     3	/// The editor's dialogs: Export… (⌘E and the toolbar button), Clip ▸ Speed…,
     4	/// Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…, and the missing-media offer a document makes when its window appears.
     5	///
     6	/// The four are one file because they are one shape — capture what the sheet needs,
     7	/// present it, and let it commit through `ProjectDocument` — and because none of
     8	/// them owns any editor state. Everything durable lives in the sheet controllers
     9	/// (`ExportSheetController`, `SpeedSheetController`, `SpeedRampSheetController`,
    10	/// `RelinkSheetController`); this is only the seam that puts them up.
    11	///
    12	/// **Every editor action is validated false while a sheet is attached**
    13	/// (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`), which is what lets a
    14	/// sheet capture a project handle and trust it: the document cannot change
    15	/// under an open dialog.
    16	extension EditorViewController {
    17	
    18	    // MARK: - Export
    19	
    20	    /// ⌘E, File ▸ Export…, and the toolbar's Export button. Refuses on an
    21	    /// empty timeline rather than opening a dialog whose only honest answer
    22	    /// is a zero-length movie.
    23	    func exportProjectCommand() {
    24	        guard let document = document, document.project.duration > 0 else {
    25	            NSSound.beep()
    26	            return
    27	        }
    28	        guard !ReelExport.presets().isEmpty else {
    29	            NSSound.beep()
    30	            return
    31	        }
    32	        playback.pause()
    33	        presentAsSheet(ExportSheetController(editor: self))
    34	    }
    35	
    36	    /// Called by `ExportSheetController` once the save panel has a
    37	    /// destination. The project handle is captured HERE rather than inside
    38	    /// the exporter so the write is of the timeline as it was confirmed —
    39	    /// handles are immutable (spec §5.5), so nothing the document does next
    40	    /// can reach the file.
    41	    ///
    42	    /// `options` is what the export asks of the RECIPE — the timecode burn-in
    43	    /// and nothing else today. It rides beside `settings` rather than inside
    44	    /// it because the two are answered by different halves of the core: the
    45	    /// settings are `rc_export_settings`' reply, and an option smuggled into
    46	    /// the override table would be ignored without a word
    47	    /// (`export_overrides.rs`) and the file reported as a success. The default
    48	    /// is no options at all, so a caller that says nothing exports what it
    49	    /// always did.
    50	    func beginExport(settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL, options: RecipeOptions = .none) {
    51	        guard let document = document else {
    52	            NSSound.beep()
    53	            return
    54	        }
    55	        playback.pause()
    56	        presentAsSheet(
    57	            ExportProgressSheetController(
    58	                project: document.project, urls: document.mediaURLs(), settings: settings,
    59	                to: url, options: options,
    60	                graphics: GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)))
    61	    }
    62	
    63	    /// Called by `ExportSheetController`'s **Add to Queue** once the save
    64	    /// panel has a destination — `beginExport`'s sibling, and the one place a
    65	    /// queued job is built (road map 2's phase 7e).
    66	    ///
    67	    /// **The project handle AND the media URLs are read HERE, at the moment
    68	    /// the destination is known, and that is the whole of what makes a queued
    69	    /// job immutable.** The handle needs no clone — handles are immutable
    70	    /// (spec §5.5) and every edit and undo makes a new one, so this one keeps
    71	    /// the timeline as it was confirmed however the document changes, and
    72	    /// `Exporter` publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key of its own so even the
    73	    /// frames the compositor serves the write come from it. `mediaURLs()` is
    74	    /// the half that would otherwise leak: it resolves each bookmark and asks
    75	    /// the filesystem whether the file is there, so a job that called it at
    76	    /// RUN time would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after it
    77	    /// was queued — the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. A job
    78	    /// therefore holds the answer and no document to ask again.
    79	    ///
    80	    /// Playback is NOT paused, unlike `beginExport`: a queued job runs behind
    81	    /// the editor by design, and the person who chose not to wait for it did
    82	    /// not ask for their preview to stop.
    83	    func enqueueExport(settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL, options: RecipeOptions = .none) {
    84	        guard let document = document else {
    85	            NSSound.beep()
    86	            return
    87	        }
    88	        ExportQueueController.shared.enqueue(
    89	            project: document.project, urls: document.mediaURLs(), settings: settings,
    90	            to: url, options: options,
    91	            graphics: GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey))
    92	        // Adding to a queue shows the queue: the job has no sheet of its own,
    93	        // so this window is the only thing that says it exists.
    94	        ExportQueueWindowController.shared.show()
    95	    }
    96	
    97	    // MARK: - Speed
    98	
    99	    /// Clip ▸ Speed…. Only `media` clips can take `set_speed` (spec §6 makes
   100	    /// it an error, not a refusal, on any other kind), so the sheet is opened
   101	    /// on that subset and refused outright when the subset is empty.
   102	    func presentSpeedSheet() {
   103	        let clips = selectedClips.filter { $0.source.hasSourceBound }
   104	        guard let document = document, !clips.isEmpty else {
   105	            NSSound.beep()
   106	            return
   107	        }
   108	        presentAsSheet(SpeedSheetController(document: document, clips: clips.map { $0.id }))
   109	    }
   110	
   111	    /// Clip ▸ Speed Ramp… (spec §11 SR-24): the speed ramp presets on the ONE
   112	    /// selected media clip. Its validator is the same test.
   113	    @objc func showSpeedRampSheet(_ sender: Any?) { presentSpeedRampSheet() }
   114	
   115	    /// Opens the sheet on the selected clip, over the in/out range when it
   116	    /// lies inside the clip and the whole clip otherwise
   117	    /// (`SpeedRampSheetController.span(of:range:)`).
   118	    func presentSpeedRampSheet() {
   119	        let clips = selectedClips
   120	        guard let document = document, clips.count == 1, let clip = clips.first,
   121	            clip.source.hasSourceBound
   122	        else {
   123	            NSSound.beep()
   124	            return
   125	        }
   126	        let span = SpeedRampSheetController.span(of: clip, range: document.inOutRange)
   127	        presentAsSheet(SpeedRampSheetController(document: document, clip: clip.id, span: span))
   128	    }
   129	
   130	    // MARK: - Missing media
   131	
   132	    /// Offers Relink… once per document, when its window first appears
   133	    /// (spec §5.6). Silent — not an alert — when nothing is missing, and it
   134	    /// stands aside for any sheet already up, so an export or a save dialog
   135	    /// is never elbowed out of the way by it.
   136	    func offerRelinkIfNeeded() {
   137	        guard let document = document, !document.missingMedia.isEmpty else { return }
   138	        guard view.window?.attachedSheet == nil else { return }
   139	        guard RelinkSheetController.markOffered(document) else { return }
   140	        presentAsSheet(RelinkSheetController(document: document))
   141	    }
   142	
   143	    // MARK: - Validation
   144	
   145	    /// The half of `validateUserInterfaceItem` this file owns. nil means "not
   146	    /// mine" and leaves the other answers alone.
   147	    func validateExportAction(
   148	        _ action: Selector, item: any NSValidatedUserInterfaceItem
   149	    ) -> Bool? {
   150	        guard let document = document else { return false }
   151	        switch action {
   152	        case #selector(exportProject(_:)):
   153	            return document.project.duration > 0
   154	        default:
   155	            return nil
   156	        }
   157	    }
   158	}

     4	/// The export card's two commits, Export… and Add to Queue, which end in a save panel and hand
     5	/// the resolved settings to the editor: `commit(queue:)` with the three button actions that
     6	/// reach it, `recipeOptions`, `suggestedName` and `panelMessage`. An extension of
     7	/// `ExportSheetController` in a file of its own, a pure move out of the controller before the
     8	/// HDR road map's export range (hdr H-0).

    10	    // MARK: - Commit
    11	
    12	    @objc func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    13	        dismiss(self)
    14	    }
    15	
    16	    /// Export… — write it now, behind a progress sheet.
    17	    @objc func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    18	        commit(queue: false)
    19	    }
    20	
    21	    /// Add to Queue — write it later, behind nothing. The SAME commit, in one
    22	    /// method, so the buttons cannot drift (road map 2's phase 7e).
    23	    @objc func queueClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
    24	        commit(queue: true)
    25	    }
    26	
    27	    /// Hands off to the save panel, then to `EditorViewController`'s
    28	    /// `beginExport` — or, for Add to Queue, its `enqueueExport`. The settings
    29	    /// are captured BEFORE the dismissal: after it this controller's window is
    30	    /// gone and its controls are on their way out of the view tree. Everything
    31	    /// above the handoff is the same for both buttons and is written once for
    32	    /// that reason: a queued job is not a second kind of export, it is this
    33	    /// one held until its turn.
    34	    private func commit(queue: Bool) {
    35	        // End any edit in a Custom field first. A mouse click on a button
    36	        // does not take the first responder from a text field, so the value
    37	        // typed there has not been committed — `controlTextDidEndEditing`,
    38	        // and the resolve it runs, fire only when the field editor resigns —
    39	        // and `resolved` still describes the size from BEFORE the edit.
    40	        // Handing the first responder to nobody makes it resign now,
    41	        // synchronously, so the read below sees the numbers on screen. A
    42	        // field whose text its formatter rejects refuses to resign; that is
    43	        // the person's to fix, so the click just beeps.
    44	        guard endSheetFieldEditing() else { return }
    45	        guard let editor = editor, let settings = resolved,
    46	              writeRefusal(for: settings) == nil, let window = editor.view.window
    47	        else {
    48	            NSSound.beep()
    49	            return
    50	        }
    51	        // Read while the controls still exist. `recipeOptions` is not part of
    52	        // `settings` and never can be: the burn-in changes the PICTURE, so it
    53	        // travels with the description of the picture rather than through the
    54	        // override table, which drops a key it does not know without a word
    55	        // (`RecipeOptions`).
    56	        let options = recipeOptions
    57	        // Remembered on the COMMIT and not on the dismissal: a card somebody
    58	        // opened, fiddled with and cancelled is not a choice they made — and
    59	        // queueing a job is as much a choice as exporting one, so both
    60	        // buttons record it.
    61	        currentChoice.remember()
    62	        let name = suggestedName(for: settings, in: editor)
    63	        dismiss(self)

    65	        let panel = NSSavePanel()

    71	            panel.allowedContentTypes = [type]
    72	        }

    74	        // panel appears once the settings card has finished leaving.
    75	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak editor] response in
    76	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url, let editor = editor else { return }

    78	            // project and its media are read on the far side of it, at the
    79	            // moment the destination is known — which for a queued job is the
    80	            // whole of what makes it immutable (`ExportQueueController`).
    81	            if queue {
    82	                editor.enqueueExport(settings: settings, to: url, options: options)

    87	    }
    88	
    89	    /// The sentence that would stop these settings (`Exporter.settingsRefusal`,
    90	    /// spec §11 #470), for the readout and for `commit`, or nil. `commit` asks
    91	    /// again because a Custom size typed and then clicked past is resolved
    92	    /// only inside that click.

    94	        guard let project = editor?.document?.project else { return nil }

    96	    }
    97	
    98	    /// What the card asks of the RECIPE rather than of the export settings —
    99	    /// today, the burn-in and nothing else.
   100	    var recipeOptions: RecipeOptions {
   101	        RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: burnInCheckbox.state == .on)
   102	    }
   103	
   104	    /// The document's name with the container's extension: `displayStem`, the
   105	    /// title with the package's own extension off and NOTHING else off, so
   106	    /// "Board v1.2" is `Board v1.2.mp4` (`ProjectDocument+DisplayStem.swift`).
   107	    private func suggestedName(for settings: ExportSettings, in editor: EditorViewController)

   109	    {

   112	    }

   117	    /// sheet's own (`Applies`, `isFrameSequence`), so a format that is
   118	    /// neither is a movie by the same reading that gave it a Size popup.
   119	    private static func panelMessage(for settings: ExportSettings) -> String {
   120	        if settings.isAudioOnly { return "Export the timeline's audio." }
   121	        if isFrameSequence(container: settings.container) {
   122	            return "Export the timeline as an animated \(settings.container.uppercased())."
   123	        }
   124	        return "Export the timeline as a movie."
   125	    }
   126	}

     3	/// The editor's dialogs: Export… (⌘E and the toolbar button), Clip ▸ Speed…,

     8	/// them owns any editor state. Everything durable lives in the sheet controllers
     9	/// (`ExportSheetController`, `SpeedSheetController`, `SpeedRampSheetController`,
    10	/// `RelinkSheetController`); this is only the seam that puts them up.
    11	///
    12	/// **Every editor action is validated false while a sheet is attached**
    13	/// (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`), which is what lets a
    14	/// sheet capture a project handle and trust it: the document cannot change
    15	/// under an open dialog.
    16	extension EditorViewController {
    17	
    18	    // MARK: - Export
    19	
    20	    /// ⌘E, File ▸ Export…, and the toolbar's Export button. Refuses on an
    21	    /// empty timeline rather than opening a dialog whose only honest answer
    22	    /// is a zero-length movie.

    24	        guard let document = document, document.project.duration > 0 else {
    25	            NSSound.beep()
    26	            return
    27	        }
    28	        guard !ReelExport.presets().isEmpty else {
    29	            NSSound.beep()
    30	            return
    31	        }
    32	        playback.pause()
    33	        presentAsSheet(ExportSheetController(editor: self))
    34	    }
    35	
    36	    /// Called by `ExportSheetController` once the save panel has a
    37	    /// destination. The project handle is captured HERE rather than inside
    38	    /// the exporter so the write is of the timeline as it was confirmed —
    39	    /// handles are immutable (spec §5.5), so nothing the document does next
    40	    /// can reach the file.
    41	    ///
    42	    /// `options` is what the export asks of the RECIPE — the timecode burn-in
    43	    /// and nothing else today. It rides beside `settings` rather than inside
    44	    /// it because the two are answered by different halves of the core: the
    45	    /// settings are `rc_export_settings`' reply, and an option smuggled into
    46	    /// the override table would be ignored without a word
    47	    /// (`export_overrides.rs`) and the file reported as a success. The default
    48	    /// is no options at all, so a caller that says nothing exports what it
    49	    /// always did.
    50	    func beginExport(settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL, options: RecipeOptions = .none) {
    51	        guard let document = document else {
    52	            NSSound.beep()
    53	            return
    54	        }
    55	        playback.pause()
    56	        presentAsSheet(
    57	            ExportProgressSheetController(
    58	                project: document.project, urls: document.mediaURLs(), settings: settings,
    59	                to: url, options: options,
    60	                graphics: GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)))
    61	    }
    62	
    63	    /// Called by `ExportSheetController`'s **Add to Queue** once the save
    64	    /// panel has a destination — `beginExport`'s sibling, and the one place a
    65	    /// queued job is built (road map 2's phase 7e).
    66	    ///
    67	    /// **The project handle AND the media URLs are read HERE, at the moment
    68	    /// the destination is known, and that is the whole of what makes a queued
    69	    /// job immutable.** The handle needs no clone — handles are immutable
    70	    /// (spec §5.5) and every edit and undo makes a new one, so this one keeps
    71	    /// the timeline as it was confirmed however the document changes, and
    72	    /// `Exporter` publishes it on a `RecipeSource` key of its own so even the
    73	    /// frames the compositor serves the write come from it. `mediaURLs()` is
    74	    /// the half that would otherwise leak: it resolves each bookmark and asks
    75	    /// the filesystem whether the file is there, so a job that called it at
    76	    /// RUN time would silently pick up a Relink… or a moved file from after it
    77	    /// was queued — the exact change an immutable job exists to exclude. A job
    78	    /// therefore holds the answer and no document to ask again.
    79	    ///

    81	    /// the editor by design, and the person who chose not to wait for it did
    82	    /// not ask for their preview to stop.
    83	    func enqueueExport(settings: ExportSettings, to url: URL, options: RecipeOptions = .none) {

    86	            return
    87	        }

    97	    // MARK: - Speed

    99	    /// Clip ▸ Speed…. Only `media` clips can take `set_speed` (spec §6 makes

   135	    /// is never elbowed out of the way by it.
   136	    func offerRelinkIfNeeded() {

   139	        guard RelinkSheetController.markOffered(document) else { return }

   147	    func validateExportAction(

   153	            return document.project.duration > 0
   154	        default:
   155	            return nil
   156	        }
   157	    }
   158	}

1	import AppKit
     2	
     3	/// The sheet that stays up for the write itself: a bar, a Cancel that really
     4	/// stops the session, and — once the file lands — the result and a Show in
     5	/// Finder (spec §10 step 10).
     6	///
     7	/// It owns the `Exporter`, which is why the export survives everything the
     8	/// editor does next: the sheet is retained by the presenting controller for
     9	/// as long as it is on screen, and nothing else holds the session.
    10	///
    11	/// Its own file rather than the foot of `ExportSheetController.swift`, which
    12	/// stood at 1114 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's ~600 cap. The seam is where
    13	/// the two sheets stop having anything in common: the settings card is a
    14	/// conversation with the core — every number it shows comes back from
    15	/// `rc_export_settings`, and its controls only decide what to ask for — and
    16	/// this one has already finished asking. It holds a project handle, a URL and
    17	/// an `Exporter`, watches one number climb, and turns into its own result
    18	/// panel; nothing on it can change what is being written.
    19	///
    20	/// Being a separate CLASS is what makes the cut free. `private` on an
    21	/// extension member reaches only its own file, so splitting a type across
    22	/// files costs every crossing member its privacy — the price
    23	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records paying, and the price the two `extension
    24	/// ExportSheetController` files beside this one pay. A type carries its own
    25	/// scope, so every member below keeps the visibility it had, and
    26	/// `EditorViewController+Export.swift` presenting it is the only name that
    27	/// crosses.
    28	final class ExportProgressSheetController: NSViewController {
    29	    private let exporter = Exporter()
    30	    /// The project handle as the export was confirmed. Handles are immutable
    31	    /// (spec §5.5), so edits made after this point cannot reach the file.
    32	    private let project: ReelProject
    33	    private let urls: [UInt32: URL]
    34	    private let settings: ExportSettings
    35	    private let destination: URL
    36	    /// What the export asks of the RECIPE rather than of the settings — the
    37	    /// timecode burn-in (spec §7.3, road map 2's phase 7). It is a separate
    38	    /// argument because it is a separate question: `ExportSettings` is what
    39	    /// `rc_export_settings` resolved, and an option posted through the
    40	    /// override table would be dropped in silence and the file reported a
    41	    /// success. Defaulted, so a caller that does not burn in is written the
    42	    /// way it always was.
    43	    private let options: RecipeOptions
    44	    /// The document's compiled graphics as the export was confirmed (G-13),
    45	    /// pinned by `Exporter.export` for the write.
    46	    private let graphics: GraphicSet?
    47	
    48	    private let bar = NSProgressIndicator()

`--mutant NAME` runs the selftest alone (never the sweep) and prints `MUTANT
PASS` when exactly its rows fail: `no-unlink` P2 (the unlink is skipped in
the real Preferences folder; over a scratch folder the unlink is the whole
removal, there being no daemon, so the mutant stays out of those rows),
`no-refusal` P3–P6 and not P5s (`refusal` answers None; the real folder
still asks the rule itself), `no-busy` P8 (`busy` answers None). Exit 1 on
a failed row only: a `busy` or `denied` name is reported, not failed.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import plistlib
import pwd
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

APP_DOMAIN = "com.kgalligan.FrameJob"
HARMLESS = ("NS", "Apple")                       # AppKit's key-name families
# What a probe compiled from app/Sources writes, under either name (the old one
# from an old tree's probe or harness paint, spec §11 NM-15).
FAMILIES = ("FrameJob", "Reelcut", "RC", "NS", "Apple")
KEY_PREFIXES = ("FrameJob", "Reelcut")           # the product's own keys, new and old
BUSY_MINUTES = 60

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
# The account's own home, not `$HOME`: `cfprefsd` does not follow the variable.
REAL_PREFERENCES = os.path.join(pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir, "Library", "Preferences")
WORK = os.path.join(HERE, "work")
SOURCES = HERE
SELFTEST_PREFIX = "framejob.proof-defaults-selftest."
# The proofs' probe domains, under the new names only (spec §11 NM-15).
PREFIXES = ("com.kgalligan.framejob.", "framejob.")
# The product's own executables, and its bundle-id namespaces, under both names
# (the old ones because an old-tree run still writes them, spec §11 NM-15).
EXECUTABLES = ("frame job", "frame job debug", "framejob", "framejob-agent", "framejob-mcp",
               "reelcut", "reelcut-agent", "reelcut-mcp")
NAMESPACES = ("com.kgalligan.framejob", "com.kgalligan.reelcut")
UNATTRIBUTED_NAME = re.compile(r"probe|harness|refute|spike")
SKIP_DIRS = ("node_modules", ".git", "Intermediates.noindex", "target")
SKIP_SUFFIXES = (".app", ".dSYM")
MACHO_MAGICS = {b"\xfe\xed\xfa\xce", b"\xfe\xed\xfa\xcf", b"\xce\xfa\xed\xfe",
                b"\xcf\xfa\xed\xfe", b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbe", b"\xbe\xba\xfe\xca",
                b"\xca\xfe\xba\xbf", b"\xbf\xba\xfe\xca"}
MUTANTS = ("no-unlink", "no-refusal", "no-busy")
EXPECTED = {"no-unlink": {"P2"}, "no-refusal": {"P3", "P4", "P5", "P6"}, "no-busy": {"P8"}}
MUTANT = None

_SALT = os.urandom(16)


# ---- what a session moved --------------------------------------------------------

def read_env():
    """The environment every `defaults` of this file runs in (a read, the
    recipe's delete, the selftest's write): this process's without
    `CFFIXED_USER_HOME`, so two reads of one domain answer the same thing
    whether or not the folder that variable names exists at either, and a
    delete acts on the domain its read-back reads. What the guard answers
    for is the owner's domain, the one read without the variable: an
    instance under a scratch home that exists writes it (#238), and a write
    that lands anywhere else moves nothing of the owner's."""
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("CFFIXED_USER_HOME", None)
    return env


def _export(domain, run=None):
    """`defaults export <domain> -` as a dict ({} for no such domain), or
    None when it could not be run or read. Runs in `read_env()`."""
    if not domain or domain.startswith("-"):
        return None

                       "here sets it to a scratch socket, and nothing on screen shows it",
    "RCWriteCatalog": "an argument-domain build step that writes the catalog snapshot and "
                      "exits before any window; no screen launches with it",
    "FrameJobGraphicPrefetchOff": "a measurement switch that draws every graphic on the "
                                 "compositor's queue alone; no screen shows it",
    "FrameJobGraphicKeepOff": "a measurement switch that keeps no graphic frame (spec §11 "
                             "G-37 (e)); no screen shows it",
    "FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff": "a measurement switch that sets the engine's decoded-image "
                                   "cache's limit to 0 (spec §11 G-39 (d)); no screen shows it",
    "RCDevLookGalleryDump": "a dev launch default naming a folder the Look gallery writes "
                            "its thumbnails to (look_proof.py's G rows); no screen launches "
                            "with it",
    "RCCodecProbe": "an argument-domain switch that prints the bundled encoders' versions "
                    "for codecs_proof.py; no screen launches with it",
    "RCDevExportFault": "a dev launch default that puts a fault in an export's pumps "
                        "(spec §11 #378); no screen exports",
    "RCDevVerticalSaveFault": "a dev launch default naming the copy whose save "
                              "make_vertical_version fails (#460), read only with `path`; "
                              "no screen launches with it",

            self.score(rid, "fail", f"MCP: {error}")
            return f"MCP: {error}"

        parity = parity_lines(self.out, look)
        marker = dev_marker_count(log_path(self.out, look))

                 f"{homed}",
                 f"welcome {welcome}", f"`Frame Job: ` lines {len(parity)}",
                 f"dev tools missing {missing}", f"marker count {marker} (want {len(DEV_TOOLS)})"]
        self.score(rid, "pass" if ok else "fail", "; ".join(notes))
        return None if ok else "; ".join(notes)

    def row_p2(self):
        declared = set()
        literals = set()
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(SOURCES)):
            if not name.endswith(".swift"):
                continue
            text = open(os.path.join(SOURCES, name), encoding="utf-8").read()
            declared |= set(re.findall(r'id: "([a-z]+\.[a-zA-Z._]+)", title:', text))
            literals |= set(re.findall(r'static let \w*Key = "((?:FrameJob|RC)[^"]*)"', text))
        pinned = {key for key, _ in PINS} | {APPEARANCE_KEY, ANALYSIS_HOLD[0],
                                               CAPTURE_SCALE[0]}
        problems = []
        if declared != set(SECTIONS):
            problems.append(f"sections in app/Sources but not SECTIONS "
                            f"{sorted(declared - set(SECTIONS))}, in SECTIONS but not app/Sources "
                            f"{sorted(set(SECTIONS) - declared)}")
        uncovered = sorted(k for k in literals if k not in pinned and k not in NOT_SHOWN)
        if uncovered:
            problems.append(f"keys neither pinned nor in NOT_SHOWN {uncovered}")
        stale = sorted(k for k in NOT_SHOWN if k not in literals)
        if stale:
            problems.append(f"NOT_SHOWN keys that are no such literal {stale}")

                   f"key literals: {len(literals & pinned)} pinned (one, {APPEARANCE_KEY}, "
                   f"per look), {len(literals & set(NOT_SHOWN))} not shown")

72:- **CI-4 — Mint is the action ink, and nothing else uses it.**
73-  `DS.action` (dark `#5CD6B0`, light `#1E8F6E`) with `DS.actionInk`
74-  (`#101010`) on a solid band. The Clip tab's pinned action lane REPLACES
75-  the Actions section, and actions are numbered by TIME order (start, then
76-  id), not by creation — the timeline's bands, the lane and "editing N"
77-  all count the same way (`ActionBands.ordered`).
78-- **CI-5 — The Clip tab is sub-tabs over a pinned block** (road map 9 §3,
79-  the clip inspector redesign's phase 2). Above the scroll view, and not in
80-  it, sits one block — the selection header, the action lane and a strip of
81-  sub-tabs — OWNED by the pane (`InspectorPane.pinnedBlock`, built by
82-  `makeHeader()` on every rebuild and never stacked) and HOSTED by the
83-  controller in a container between the tab strip and the scroll view. The
84-  tabs follow the selection's kinds: Text for an all-text selection, Shape
85-  for an all-shape one, Picture when a selected clip draws pixels, Sound
86-  when one has audio, and Clip ALWAYS, last; Text and Shape come first. The
87-  default is the first tab, so a text clip opens on Text. A tab picked by
88-  hand is KEPT while an action is selected or changed and is FORGOTTEN by
89-  the controller whenever the selection's ids change, whatever tab is
90-  showing (`refresh(isLive:)`'s `ids != lastSelection` block calls
91-  `ClipPane.forgetSubTab()`), so A → B → A comes back on the default. Each
92-  tab lists its own sections (spec §4.3), and the open rule applies per
93-  tab: on a tab with no expanded section the first one with no stored
94-  preference opens. Section ids — the `UserDefaults` keys — are unchanged;
    /// the number that matters is the over.
    static var meterFill: NSColor { clipAudio }
    static var meterTrough: NSColor { .quaternaryLabelColor }
    static var meterClip: NSColor { coral }

    /// The action ink (spec §11 CI-4): bands, the lane, the selected span's
    /// washes and "editing N" — and nothing else. Mint in dark, a deeper
    /// green in light, where the design has only settled the ink.
    static let action = NSColor(name: nil) { appearance in
        let dark = appearance.bestMatch(from: [.darkAqua, .aqua]) == .darkAqua
        return dark
            ? NSColor(srgbRed: 0x5C / 255, green: 0xD6 / 255, blue: 0xB0 / 255, alpha: 1)
            : NSColor(srgbRed: 0x1E / 255, green: 0x8F / 255, blue: 0x6E / 255, alpha: 1)
    }
    /// Text on a SOLID action band.
    static let actionInk = NSColor(
        srgbRed: 0x10 / 255, green: 0x10 / 255, blue: 0x10 / 255, alpha: 1)
    /// The timeline's action lane under the name strip, by track size S/M/L.
    static let actionLaneHeights: [CGFloat] = [5, 12, 18]

    // MARK: - Type

Settings (Frame Job ▸ Settings…) has four sections, one under the other: MCP,
Assistant, Transcription and Playback. The first is where a person finds how to connect
an MCP client such as Claude Code to Frame Job (spec §11 MC-7); the second is
where they give Frame Job an Anthropic API key, choose the model for the
Assistant tab, and set how a long conversation is kept in bounds; the third is
where they give it an AssemblyAI API key, so that the Generate Captions sheet
can transcribe in the cloud instead of on this Mac; the fourth is where they
say whether Frame Job draws a window's graphics ahead while it is left alone
(spec §11 G-38).

The "MCP" section opens with its bold heading alone, with no ⓘ. Under it, two
short paragraphs in 13 pt black (white in dark), visible rather than in a
popover: "An MCP client such as Claude Code uses Frame Job's tools through
framejob-mcp, a helper inside this app. It reaches Frame Job over a local socket
that only programs you run can open." and "If Frame Job isn't running, the first
tool call opens it in the background. To add Frame Job to Claude Code, copy the
command and run it in Terminal." Then the helper's path inside this copy of
the app, ending `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`, in 12 pt monospace black,
selectable, wrapping by character when it is long. Then a "Copy MCP Command"
button (a white square button with a thin outline), and under it an empty
status line: after a press it reads "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press
Return.", and in a copy of Frame Job without the helper the button is dimmed and
the line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." Nothing in
the section is selected when the window opens; the Anthropic key field has the
focus.

The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections each open with their bold heading
and, just after it, a small mid-grey ⓘ icon about the height of the heading's capitals, darkening while the pointer
is on it. Resting on an ⓘ for about a third of a second opens a standard macOS
popover under it — the rounded bubble with an arrow (spec §11 SH-5) — holding
that section's explanation in 13 pt black (white in dark), in short
paragraphs; leaving the icon closes it, and clicking the icon opens it and
keeps it open until it is clicked again or a click lands elsewhere. The
popover is not in the capture: it opens only under the pointer or a click,
and nothing in the catalog hovers or clicks.

Under the "Assistant" heading: an "Anthropic API key:" field, empty, whose
placeholder reads "Paste your key"; a "Model:" field, empty, whose grey
placeholder reads "claude-opus-5-5" (the default when it is left blank); then
the chat settings, two rows of their own. The first is a ticked checkbox

# Objections: Tips plan

Checked against `/Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-tips` at 34c7fea2 (clean). The plan's "What
is true now" held everywhere I read it (toolbar row, `AccentButton(fill:)`, the two person doors,
the queue's `enqueue`/`finished`/`job(_:)`, the pane loop and the three probe rows that count
panes, the inventory's token-and-function match, `mcp.defaults_moved`). The schedule arithmetic
(O1-O3, S1-S10) is consistent with the request. Six objections, worst first.

## 1. The automatic ask's wiring has no row that can fail

**Claim.** Item 3's chain from a finished Export… to the dialog (`onSuccess` called in the
`.success` arm, `TipsDoors.exportSucceeded` counting, waiting for the sheet to end, `takeAsk`,
`showAutomatic`) is run by no row; the proof stays green with the chain dead or wrong.

**Evidence.**
- Delete the planned `onSuccess?()` line from `ExportProgressSheetController.finished`, or put
  it in the `.failure` arm (which also serves a cancel, `:209-219`): T1 only greps
  `TipsDoors.exportSucceeded(` in `EditorViewController+Export.swift`, A1/A2 call `TipsAsk`
  directly, C1 calls `showAutomatic()` directly, F1-F3 call the follower with an injected
  closure. Every row passes; no mutant names this.
- Same for the body of `TipsDoors.exportSucceeded(sheetOn:)` and `follow(queueJob:)`: they are
  built on `TipsAsk.shared` / `TipsWindowController.shared` and no row calls them. "Ask at
  success instead of at sheet end" and "never ask" both pass.
- L2 (agent `export` leaves no Tips window, no key moved) passes on the tree before any code
  and is never seen failing: mutants are probe rebuilds, so `agent-follows` is held by T1's
  tree text alone.
- The only end-to-end check is the `defaults write` row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which a
  script can do: probes already run a real export through this sheet presented as
  `beginExport` presents it (`tools/proof/docs_bugs_b4_probe.swift:179`,
  `ai_docs_b2_probe.swift:132`).

**Suggested change.** Give `TipsDoors` its ask and window by injection (defaulting to the
shared ones) and add a probe row that runs a real `ExportProgressSheetController` export with
due state: nothing before the sheet ends, the window visible and last-asked written after, and
nothing on a cancelled or failed export, with a `success-unwired` mutant on the `onSuccess?()`
line.

## 2. C1's "not key" check passes for either door

**Claim.** O5's safety decision (the automatic ask never takes key, so Return cannot press
"Leave a Tip") is checked by a row that reads the same whichever method runs, and has no mutant.

**Evidence.** `app/Sources/EditorWindow.swift:272-275`: "a probe's window is never key, so its
key-window rows set [`keyWindowStandIn`]". In the probe process `show()` (key and front) also
leaves `isKeyWindow` false, so C1's "`showAutomatic()` leaves it visible and not key" would
pass with `showAutomatic()` calling `makeKeyAndOrderFront`. The ten mutants include none for
this ordering.

**Suggested change.** Make the ordering observable (the controller takes its two order calls as
closures, or the row activates the probe as `cursor_keys_proof.swift:111` does and asserts
`show()` IS key and `showAutomatic()` is NOT), with an `auto-takes-key` mutant, and record in
TIP-7 why the set passes ten or drop one of the threshold pair.

## 3. `screens.py` P2 fails on the three state keys

**Claim.** The plan pins only `FrameJobTips` in `screens.py`; the other three new keys are left
uncovered and P2 fails the catalog run.

**Evidence.** `tools/proof/screens.py:1326-1337`: P2 collects every
`static let \w*Key = "(FrameJob|RC)…"` literal in `app/Sources` and fails with "keys neither
pinned nor in NOT_SHOWN" for any not in `PINS` or `NOT_SHOWN` (`:255-257`). The plan's own
mould declares keys exactly that way (`BackgroundRender.swift:9,11`, `enabledKey`,
`delayKey`), so `FrameJobTipsExports`, `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` and `FrameJobTipsLastAsked`
land in the scan. `screens.py` is not in `make gate`, so nothing reports it until the next
catalog run.

**Suggested change.** Add the three keys to `NOT_SHOWN` with their reason (read and written
only when an export a person confirmed completes; no screen exports) in the same change, and
name it in the plan's instrument list.

## 4. L1 and L2 depend on the owner's toggle in the shared domain

**Claim.** The live rows read `FrameJobTips` from the bundle's real defaults domain unless the
launch pins it, and only L3's launch is said to.

**Evidence.** The plan runs `tips_proof.py` against Release, whose domain is the owner's own
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` (root `CLAUDE.md`, "A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults
domain"). The toggle exists so the owner can untick it; once he has, L1 ("a visible Tips right
of Export…") fails on every run with nothing wrong in the tree. The plan guards `screens.py`
against exactly this (`("FrameJobTips", True)`) but says nothing for L1/L2's instances.

**Suggested change.** Launch L1's and L2's instance with `-FrameJobTips YES` (argument domain,
as L3 uses `NO`), and say so in the row text.

## 5. Four documents the change makes false are not in the plan's list

**Claim.** The plan edits `reference/settings.mdx`, `editor-window.mdx` and
`remembered-choices.mdx:141` but leaves other lines that count Settings' sections or place
Export… last.

**Evidence.**
- `docs/site/src/content/docs/assistant/set-up.mdx:27`: "the second of the window's four
  sections".
- `docs/site/src/data/features.json:20350`: "in four sections: MCP, Assistant, Transcription
  and Playback" (the plan adds rows but does not name this summary).
- `docs/site/src/content/docs/export/export-sheet.mdx:15,23`: "The accent Export… button at the
  right end of the toolbar" (Tips is right of it by default).
- `docs/manual-checks.md:447`: "a display shorter than its four panes".

**Suggested change.** Add these four to the document list (a `rg -n "four (panes|sections)|right end of the toolbar"`
over `docs/` and `designs/screens/` finds them).

## 6. In the light look the button's green is the action ink's green

**Claim.** O7 keeps CI-4 by token name only; in light the two colours are near-identical, and
the plan does not say so to the owner or in TIP-6.

**Evidence.** `Theme.swift:40` `DS.forest` = `#1F8564`; `Theme.swift:118-123` `DS.action` in
light = `#1E8F6E` (10/255 apart in two channels). CI-4
(`designs/spec/11-decisions/chrome-inspector-keys.md:72`): "Mint is the action ink, and nothing
else uses it."

**Suggested change.** State in O7 and TIP-6 that the toolbar button's green matches the action
ink in the light look and that TIP-6 accepts it for this experiment (amending CI-4 by ID), or
pick a green that is apart from it in both looks.

verdict: revise
